body:
The bug is still present in v4.7 and v4.8 [3756fbb2c]. The problem is caused by these lines:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00462d686e310710896ed88596fb267a8ce16b8b/scene/gui/spin_box.cpp#L323-L327
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00462d686e310710896ed88596fb267a8ce16b8b/scene/gui/spin_box.cpp#L343-L344

The spinbox always cedes focus to its inner line edit on interaction with either mouse button. If the spinbox is in click focus mode, this means it will gain focus just to instantly lose it, and repeated clicks of the non-line edit area of the spinbox (including the small area which is occupied by neither the lined edit or the arrows, see the video) will keep passing focus back and forth.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01ea004a-173a-4170-ad2a-1a98f3bcd85e

For an immediate workaround, as long as the spinbox has focus mode = NONE, the line edit's focus state and the spinbox's focus state are essentially equivalent and one can use the line edit's focus_entered/exited signals as proxies for the spinbox's.

I'd like to work on this.

The diagnosis in the thread points at `scene/gui/spin_box.cpp` around the line-edit focus handling: focus is transferred between the SpinBox's inner `LineEdit` and its arrow buttons, and `focus_exited` is emitted (or suppressed) per inner control instead of once when focus actually leaves the composite widget — so clicking from the SpinBox to a Button never produces the signal a caller needs to commit the value.

My plan is to reproduce with a minimal scene, make `SpinBox` emit `focus_exited` only when focus leaves the control as a whole while leaving `focus_entered` and line-edit editing behaviour unchanged, and add a test scene under `tests/scene/gui/` covering tab-away, click-to-another-control, and click-between-internal-parts. PR to follow.
